I am a Linux developer learning eBPF and want a practical tutorial. Explain the execution model and the relationship between a BPF program, the kernel verifier, maps, and attachment points. Describe how a user-space process loads an object file, configures the program, and reads results. Make clear which work runs in the kernel and which work runs in user space.

Please build the explanation around an example that counts process executions. Show a minimal CO-RE C program using a tracepoint, a map keyed by process ID, and the necessary license declaration. Explain how to compile it using clang, generate or obtain vmlinux.h, and load it using libbpf or an appropriate bpftool workflow. Include the commands as illustrative examples, and explain how privileges and kernel configuration affect them.

Then discuss verifier constraints including bounded loops, initialized memory, valid pointer ranges, and stack size. Explain how to inspect verifier errors and distinguish a verifier rejection from an attachment failure. Cover the lifetime of maps and links, cleanup when a loader exits, and why pinning may be useful. Include a short section about how to test safely on a development machine, avoid collecting sensitive information, and measure the performance overhead of instrumentation.

I would also like examples of alternative attachment points such as kprobes, tracepoints, XDP, and cgroup hooks, along with situations in which each is useful. Briefly compare ring buffers and perf event buffers for sending events to user space. Explain how BTF and CO-RE improve portability and what they do not guarantee across different kernels. Mention how to check whether a kernel provides the features that the sample requires.

Finally, suggest three exercises that progressively extend the example: first count events by command name, then filter by a configurable process ID, and finally stream a timestamped event to a user-space consumer. Explain how to verify the results and point out common mistakes. Write for an experienced systems programmer who knows C but has never written eBPF. Keep the examples internally consistent and define unfamiliar terms when they first appear.

As a separate troubleshooting guide, describe what to inspect when the program compiles successfully but no events appear. Include checking that the selected tracepoint exists, confirming the loaded program is attached, checking map contents and looking for lost events. Discuss how the loader and the kernel communicate errors and why silently ignoring return codes can mislead the reader. Explain the difference between observing a process starting and reliably identifying a completed executable image. If kernel interfaces differ between releases, explain how to investigate the local machine instead of assuming a fixed layout. Include a brief checklist of prerequisites before the first command and a final list of further experiments.
